items.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022
items.q: When you took over the group... I have to give Mr. Herman a lot of credit... the reason why I stayed there for all of those years is because everybody came in... he would just approve it every time.

ctx.x: Yes I was going to say at 40 years some musicians have said I’ve had enough of this. And so you were launched onto another part of your career which lasted a long time.

Well you know it was a thing which I enjoyed right on through. Woody was, you know I was close to his vintage, one thing actually. And we did a lot of things together, you know a lot of restaurants I did. He and I would get restaurants and I’d tell him you know they were good and let’s go. And everything was pretty well — I even cooked for him actually. On the road I was fed up with all the [inaudible]. You had the Coleman case and I would carry a saute pan with a three-quarter pot, I mean a three gallon pot and…
Aw. I bet they appreciated that you were like the, you were one of the older guys in the band I would assume.

items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER: There's two guys I just want to talk about because they've been with you so long, now. And one is Frank Tiberi. What is it, one decade about now, isn't it? INTERVIEWEE: It's ten years, yeah.

ctx.x: To be able to play a ballad and play it on all kinds of peoples' programs and --
And what I understand, too, from Frank Tiberi, that he was an eager learner, always open to --
